newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses up with Dow, Paris hits record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses up with Dow, Paris hits record.

text.p: European stock markets opened stronger on Wednesday, with France's CAC-40 index racing to a record high in early trade following Wall Street big gains overnight.

In currency markets, the dollar was climbing back above 113 yen after tumbling overnight following the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan survey which showed large manufacturers growing surprisingly optimistic in June.

The blue chip CAC-40 index jumped nearly two percent in heavy volume to score a record high at 2,836.14 points. The CAC's gains came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 153.80 points overnight to close at 7,758.06, the third largest gain in point terms this year.
Two-thirds of New York's gains were made in the final 90 minutes of trading, which helped erase most of Monday's 192-point loss on worries Japanese investors would sell their U.S. assets.
In Paris, Compagnie Bancaire's buy-out offer for Cardif CDF.PA and Locabail units also boosted French shares.
The offer marks Cie Bancaire's move from a holding company to an operational company, said the head of equities sales at a large French brokerage firm.
At 0930 GMT, Cie Bancaire shares were off their high but still up 6.98 percent at 736 francs.

London's FTSE-100 index also opened higher, but its rise was more restrained ahead of the first budget of Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on July 2 and a government debt auction.
The UK was due to auction two billion sterling 10-year gilts, with results due at 1015 GMT. Auction results will provide clues to the near-term interest-rate outlook.

"Wall Street will give a reasonable tone to the market this morning, and the gilts auction will be a test of sentiment," said NatWest equity strategist David McBain. "But until we get rid of the clouds surrounding Gordon Brown's maiden budget, we'll not make any great progress."
Germany's DAX index was up nearly one percent in early trading, with investors looking for a test of its record high at 3,798.94 reached on June 20.

In currency markets, the Japanese central bank's June diffusion index for big manufacturers, a key guage of business confidence, rose to plus seven from plus two in March and compared with analysts' forecasts for a fall of 0.5.
The dollar shed a yen overnight on the report, but analysts expected losses to be limited because optimism slipped among smaller firms to minus seven in June from minus six in March.
"The headline number may say one thing, but the underlying numbers point to the fact that the domestic economy remains depressed," said Lee Ferridge, Commerzbank currency strategist.

"The only sector that saw a big pick-up was major manufacturers. They are the exporters so, the tankan highlights that Japan is still relying on increasing exports and its domestic economy is going nowhere at the moment."
CURRENCIES AT 0940 GMT
The dollar was at 113.87 yen and 1.7213 marks, compared with 114.75 yen and 1.7235 marks in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0940 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 33.5 points at 4,629.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 52.72 points at 2,837.48.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 32.24 points at 3,788.06.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was quoted at $338.00 in early trade against $338.90 at the close on Monday. Silver was at $4.78, down from $4.81 in late Monday trade.
